newsitem.title: DUBAI: Boost demand to beat excess capacity says SIA.
newsitem.headline: Boost demand to beat excess capacity says SIA.

text.p: Singapore Airlines cargo chief Huang Cheng Eng said passenger and combined passenger/cargo airlines should boost demand to overcome present excess airfreight capacity in order to deal with "plunging yields".
"It is too late to do anything about capacity. The challenge is to accelerate demand," he told the 18th Air Cargo Forum meeting here on Monday.
One way of stimulating demand was to offer some time definitive products, which would require closer cooperation between forwarders and the airlines, in both exporting and importing countries.

At the right price "this could draw a a vast amount of cargo shipped by sea.... at present only two to three percent of cargo(by volume) goes by air. If we could just double that figure, the industry would no have problems," he added.
Eng said that in 1990 there were only six full freighters operators in Asia and this figure has now doubled.

"In other regions, airlines are turning to freighters to boost their bottom line. But too many airlines are entering the business simultaneously. There is excess capacity and this has wreaked havoc with yields, " Eng added.
"But these airlines are still overwhelmingly passenger airlines and they are not really looking at cargo."

However he said that express and dedicated all-cargo airlines would continue to be "niche market players" and that the lion's share of the global cargo business will continue to be the business of passenger and combi-airlines.
